Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 1) Find the rate of interest if the amount after 2 years of simple interest on capital of tk. 1200 is tk 1440 -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Amount,A = Tk.1440
Principal,P = Tk.1200
Interest, I= TK. (1440 − 1200) = 240

R = (240 × 100)/(1200 × 2) = 10%

Alternatively, We can go through a thought process
i.e.1200 == 20% ↑ (240 in 2 years) ⇒ 1440
That means 10% rise in each year.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 2) Find the compound interest on Tk 1000 at the rate of 20% per annum for 18 month when interest is compounded half yearly.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Given,Principal,P = tk. 1000
Compound rate,R = 20%per annum
= 20/2
= 10% half-yearly
Time = 18 month
= 3 half - years

Amount,A = {P × [1 + (R/100)]n}
= {1000 × [1 + (10/100)]3}
= (1000 × 11 × 11 × 11) ÷ (10 × 10 × 10)
A = tk.1331
Hence, compound interest = tk.1331

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 3) In what time will Tk. 3300 become Tk. 3399 at 6% per annum interest compounded half-yearly?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
P = Tk.3300
A = Tk.3399
R = 6% per annum

Let the time be n years.

Compound Interest Is Taken Half yearly.

A = P × [1 + (R/2/100)]2n
3399 = 3300(1 + 3/100)2n
(1.03)2n = 3399/3300
(1.03)2n = (1.03)1
Thus,
2n = 1year
n = 1/2 year
= 6 months

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 4) A sum becomes 4 times at simple interest in 10 years. What is the rate of interest?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Here, the sum becomes 4 times that means 100, becomes 400.
Rate of such question is given by
R = interest/time = 300/10 = 30%

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 5) A sum of money placed at compound interest doubles itself in 4 years. In how many years will it amount to 8 times?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let,
Principal = Tk. 100
Amount = Tk. 200

Alternative Method:
Suppose 100 be the principal.
In 4 years it doubles and becomes 200.
In next 4 years 200 double to 400.
In next 4 years 400 doubles to 800.
Hence the period for 8 times is 12 years.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 6) If the compound interest in the third year at 8% per annum on a certain sum is Tk 3600, then what is the difference between the compound interest in the 4th and 5th year?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Compound interest for the 4th year = 3600 + (3600 × 8 × 1)/100.
= 3600 + 288.
= Tk. 3888.

Compound interest for the 5th year = 3888 + (3888 × 8 × 1)/100.
= 3888 + 311.04.
= Tk. 4199.04.

Difference between the compound interest in the 4th and 5th year = 4199.04 - 3888.
= Tk. 311.04.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 7) A sum of money doubles itself in 10 years. How many years will it take to triple itself?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let P = 100,
A = 200,
It means I = 100

Now We want A = 300,
means I = 200
Years for I of Tk. 100 = 10
Years for I of Tk. 200 = (10/100) × 200 = 20 Years

Alternative Method:
Assuming simple interest, let the amount be P and rate of interest per annum be R%.

Given that P becomes 2P in 10 years.
=> P + PX10X R/100 = 2P
=> 1 + R/10 = 2
=> R = 10

Let P triple itself in N years:
=> P + PXNX 10/100 = 3P
=> 1 + N/10 = 3
=> N = 20 years

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 8) The present value of a machine is Tk. 10000 and its value depreciates every year by 10%. What will be its value after 2 years?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
If the value of the machine at the beginning of year 1 is 10,000 and then it reduces by 10%, the value of the machine at the end of year 1 is:
10,000 × (100%-10%) = 9,000
And again, at the end of Year 2, we follow a similar route:
9000 × (100% - 10%)
= 8,100

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 9) The original cost of a machine is Tk. 10,000. If the annual depreciation is 10%, after how many years will it be valued at Tk. 6,561?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Cost of machine 10000/-
Depreciation 10% each year.
1st year = 10000 - 1000 = 9000/-
2nd year = 9000 - 900 = 8100/-
3rs year = 8100 - 810 = 7290/-
4th year = 7290 - 729 = 6561/-
Depreciation will be deducted from the amount left after subtracting previous depreciation value.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 10) A sum of money becomes 8/5 of itself in 5 years at a certain rate of interest. What is the rate of the interest?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the sum of money be P(which is the principal value) and rate of interest be R.
According to the question,
Amount (principal +simple interest) = 8P/5
Time (T) = 5 years
Simple interest (SI) = PRT/100
SI = 5PR/100
Amount = P + SI
8P/5 = P + (5PR/100)
8P/5 = P(100 + 5R)/100
160 = 100 + 5R
5R = 60
R = 12
Therefore, rate of interest = 12% p.a.

Alternative Method:
Given A = 8/5p (8/5 of the sum) .
Time = 5years .
Let the sum be P = 100.
Then, the amount = 8/5p = (value of p is 100)
= 8/5 × 100
= 160 .
S. I. = A-P
= 160 - 100
= 60 .
Hence,
Rate = S.I. × 100/P × T
= 60 × 100/100 × 5
= 12% p.a.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 13) By investing in 16(2/3)% stock at 64, one earns Tk.1500. The investment made is:
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
To earn Tk.50/3, investment = Tk. 64.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 14) The stock he bought which was 6% of face value now worth 8% of the market value.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let x be the market value,
we don't know face value so consider 100.
6% of 100 = 8% of x.
(6/100) × 100 = (8/100) × x.
6 = 8x/100.
x = 600/8.
x = 75.

Alternative Solution:
For an income of Tk. 8, investment = Tk. 100.
For an income of Tk. 6, investment = Tk.(100/8 × 6) = Tk. 75
Market value of Tk. 100 stock = Tk. 75.

= 540

Tk (12/100 × 5400) = Tk. 648

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 16) Tk. 9800 are invested partly in 9% stock at 75 and 10% stock at 80 to have an equal amount of income. The investment in 9% stock is:
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the investment in 9% stock be Tk x.
Then, investment in 10% stock = Tk. (9800 - x).
(9/75) × X = 10/80 × (9800 - X)
3X/25 = (9800 - X)/8
24X = 9800 × 25 × -25X
49X = 9800 × 25
X = 5000

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 17) By investing Tk. 1620 in 8% stock, Mizan earns Tk. 135. The stock is then quoted at:
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
To earn Tk. 135, investment = Tk. 1620.
To earn Tk. 8, investment = Tk.(1620/135 × 8)
= Tk 96
So, Market value of Tk. 100 stock = Tk. 96.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 18) A 12% stock yielding 10% is quoted at:
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
To earn Tk. 10, money invested = Tk. 100.
To earn Tk. 12, money invested = Tk (100/10 × 12)
= Tk. 120.
Market value of Tk.100 stock = Tk. 120.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 19) A man buys Tk. 25 shares in a company which pays 9 % dividend. The money invested is such that it gives 10 % on investment. At what price did he buy the shares?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Suppose he buys each share for Tk. x.
Then, Tk.(25 × 9/100) = (x × 10/100)
or x = Tk. 22.50.
Cost of each share = Tk. 22.50.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 20) Find the income on 7(½) % stock of Tk. 2000 purchased at Tk. 80.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Face Value of the stock = Tk.2000
Dividend is 7(1/2)% = 15/2% of the face value
Dividend = (2000 × 15) ÷ (2 × 100)
= Tk. 150

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 21) To produce an annual income of TK. 800 from a 8% stock at 90, the amount of stock needed is:
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Since face value is not given, take it as Tk.100.
As it is an 8% stock, income (dividend) per stock = Tk.8
ie, For an income of Tk. 8, amount of stock needed = Tk.100
For an income of Tk.800, amount of stock needed = (100 × 800)/8
= 10000

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 22) A man invested tk. 1500 in a stock at 95 to obtain an income of tk. 130. What is the dividend from the stock?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
By investing Tk. 1500, the man obtained an income of Tk. 130.
So, by investing Tk. 95, the income will be = (130/1500) × 96
= Tk 8.32
So, the divided = 8.32%

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 23) A company issued 25000 shares of par value tk. 15 each. If the company has decided to give the dividend tk. 30000, what is the rate of dividend paid by the company?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Number of shares = 25000
Face value of each share = Tk. 15
Let R be the rate of interest.

Dividend per share = 15 × R/100
Total dividend = 25000 × 15 × R/100
As per the question: 25000 × 15 × R/100
= 30000
R = 30000/3750 = 8

So, the dividend is 8%.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 24) Merun invested Tk. 333000 in 5(½) % stocks at 110. If brokerage is TK. 1, what is his annual income from his investment?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Investment = Tk. 333000
Since face value is not given, we can take it as Tk. 100
and dividend per share = Tk.11/2
Market Value = 110 + 1 = 111
Number of shares purchased = 333000/111 = 3000
Total income = 3000 × 11/2 = Tk.16500

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 25) Find the income of 8% stock of Tk.1200 purchased at Tk.120 -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Face Value = Tk.1200
Market Value = Tk.120
Dividend (income) = (1200 × 8)/100
= Tk.96

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 26) A man bought 20 shares of Tk. 50 at 5 discount, the rate of dividend being 13(1/2). The rate of interest obtained is:
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Investment = Tk.[20 × (50 − 5)] = Tk. 900.
FaceValue = Tk. (50 × 20) = Tk.1000.
Dividend = Tk. (27/2 × 1000/100) = Tk.135.
Interest Obtained = (135/900 × 100)% = 15%

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 27) In order to obtain an income of Tk. 650 from 10% stock at Tk. 96, one must make an investment of:
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
To obtain Tk. 10, investment = Tk. 96.
To obtain Tk. 650,
Investment = Tk. (96/10 × 650) = Tk. 6240

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 28) What is the difference between the compound interests on Tk. 5000 for 1 (1/2) years at 4% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
C.I. when interest compound yearly = Tk. [5000 × (1 + 4/100) (1 + 1/2 × 4/100)]
= Tk. 5304.
C.I. when interest is compounded half-yearly = Tk. 5000 (1 + 2/100)3
= Tk. 5306.04
Difference = Tk. (5306.04 - 5304)
= Tk. 2.04

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: 29) The population of a town was 3600 three years back. It is 4800 right now. What will be the population three years down the line, if the rate of growth of population has been constant over the years and has been compounding annually?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
The population grew from 3600 to 4800 in 3 years.
That is a growth of 1200 on 3600 during a three year span.
Therefore, the rate of growth for three years has been constant.

The rate of growth during the next three years will also be the same.
Therefore, the population will grow from 4800 by 4800 × 1/3 = 1600
Hence, the population three years from now will be 4800 + 1600 = 6400
